start: ^Is this Song Zhinian? I will question you about the banquet and the Kalaviṅka incident; you must answer truthfully without concealment.
^You started approaching Miss Yue Ling months ago; what was your intention?
Node0: ^What do you mean? Miss Yue Ling has a captivating voice and is sincere and humble. What man wouldn’t be enchanted? I simply appreciate her sincerely, which led to some private interactions.

^Who would have thought it would be caught on camera by a newspaper and reported widely? ...Ah, it disrupted my life. Miss Yue Ling has long been used to being in the spotlight, but during that time, it made my outings quite inconvenient; I was scrutinized everywhere I went.

^...And haven’t you heard? It was Miss Yue Ling who reached out to me first. As a gentleman, how could I let a lady feel sad? Besides, she is so beautiful and gentle, so I could only take time out of my busy schedule to accompany her more.
^<color=red>(I remember there is evidence that can prove his motives are impure.)</color>
Evidence0: ^That sounds nice. You’ve toiled in the National Justice Party for years; although you have some achievements, without a family background to support you, you remain an unknown to the upper echelons. Being on the newspaper with Miss Yue Ling seemed like overnight fame, leading to public discussion and attention from the higher-ups in the National Justice Party.

^Moreover, as you said, it appears Miss Yue Ling is entangled with you, making you seem both open and charming. Using a scandal with a popular singer to gain notoriety and expand your influence, Mr. Song, you’re quite the strategist!
^...Hmph, well, you’ve discovered this; I’m impressed!

^The internal party struggles are ceaseless; today, the east wind prevails, and tomorrow the west wind will triumph... Ordinary people without background are like delicate hanging plants; they can easily break with a little misstep.

^I’ve worked diligently, accumulating some achievements with my bare hands, but... it’s too slow this way. If I hope for a turn of fortune, who knows how long I’ll have to wait! Hmph, by then, I’m afraid I’ll be old and decrepit.
Node1: ^I’m clever enough to realize quickly... what I need to do is leverage this. Whether it’s Miss Yue Ling or He Renshu, they are just means to an end for me, no different at all.
^<color=red>(I remember there is evidence that can prove his feelings for Yue Ling are different.)</color>
Evidence1: ^If that’s the case, why did you keep her handkerchief close to you at the engagement banquet?
^...You’re quite troublesome; you discovered that too?
^Miss Yue Ling was born in humble circumstances but possesses strong vitality and ambition, which is why she is now famous throughout the country... I merely see my own reflection in her.
^That day, I kept this handkerchief as a memento to remind myself of how I fought my way up from the bottom. Lower-ranked individuals can be so easily discarded; I must always strive upward!
^..By the way, how did you discover the secret of my handkerchief?
^Because you didn’t die from an accident.
^The one who knows the secrets is the one who will end your life.

c-0: ^You’re right about one thing; you certainly did not die from a “small accident.” Your lifespan has indeed come to an end today.
c-1: ^The one who knows all these hidden details is also the one who will conclude your life.
g-0: ^Every grievance has its source, and every debt has its owner. Do you remember what you did that day?

Node2: ^...That day... when the banquet started, there were the usual formalities, and the attending officials... General Bai, Commander Fu, Director Rong... Minister He... they should have been properly entertained.
^...Later, after drinking a bit too much, when I went to the terrace to sober up, I didn’t see anyone lying in ambush... Besides, how could anyone predict that I would go to that corner?
^<color=red>(I remember there is evidence that is a direct cause of his death.)</color>
Evidence2: ^...This is the glass of wine for Yue Ling, right? He was caught? He really wasn’t careful; he can’t even handle small matters... Could it be that...
^Yes, your servant was discovered by Jin Wu.

c-0: ^You acted so ruthlessly toward Yue Ling; he certainly wouldn’t sit idly by. He just held back at that time. How ridiculous for someone as shrewd as you to think you had succeeded just because you had a drink before the banquet! When Jin Wu passed by, you happened to be alone on the terrace.
^Jin Wu?! That guy who relies on women for a living?
^It must be more than that; does he have feelings for Yue Ling...?

^My lord, drugging Yue Ling may seem ruthless, but it was actually for her long-term benefit. She’s in a complex situation, treated as a cash cow by that scoundrel Jin Wu, forced to expose herself daily and losing her sense of self. Perhaps, this was her chance for true freedom.
^Still arguing! Black and White Spirit Wardens! Take him to the Hometown-looking Platform!

^Did you see? Your former office already belongs to someone else, and even the achievements you accumulated have been eaten away by the internal party struggles. You still talk about wanting to achieve lasting accomplishments... In just a few months, you’ve already been forgotten by the public.

^Not true! There are still good stories about you among the people, saying that General Song jumped off a building to die for his fiancée after her death. Though his accomplishments are few, he is still seen as a romantic figure, truly loyal and emotional. Even I, White, am moved to hear it.
^What’s going on?! Why has it turned out like this?
^In all this, the one who benefits the most is the one who intervened. With all these twists and turns, doesn’t General Song understand?
^...Is it from the He family? From what I understand, they should have pinned the blame on Yue Ling...
^Indeed, they are family. However, Jin Wu has been sent back to the living world by the boss, and he wouldn’t allow Yue Ling’s reputation to be damaged.
^Therefore, he reached an agreement with the He family to testify, covering up the case as a poisoning incident caused by party strife, while you became the martyr for He Renshu.

^For the He family, this not only preserved He Renshu’s reputation but also gave He Zhi a reason to eliminate dissenters. In fact, it has won you accolades as well... but I wonder if General Song is pleased with this reputation?
^...Everything... is meaningless now. My schemes, my reputation... my future...
^At least you’ve become a wise ghost. Go back!
^I will judge you based on your crimes. Do you have any objections?

HasProblem: ^Hmm... it seems this is not the right evidence; I need to think more carefully.
